acceptance_criteria: A test proves a modified manifest without re-registration is REJECTED at load time, before any script text executes (observable-side-effect proof, not just an error return)
An end-to-end test proves the manifest hash flows into LuaScriptAudit's actual persisted audit row for a successful execution
A test proves a computed-hash/registered_hash mismatch still yields LuaScriptAudit's own {:manifest_hash_mismatch, ...} error and writes no audit row
Manifest.compute_hash/2 is the single source of the hash byte-layout formula -- executor.ex reuses it, does not duplicate the logic
Moduledoc states the hash algorithm and exactly which bytes/fields it covers
Moduledoc names any R-Co manifest.zig field deliberately not ported, framed as an open question given the source is unavailable
At least 2 scripts/test_parallel.sh full-suite runs quoted, not just one file's tests

result.notes:
Implemented Letflow.Engine.Lua.Manifest (lib/letflow/engine/lua/manifest.ex, new): struct {script_id, capabilities} reusing Letflow.Engine.Lua.Capabilities.capability() directly (not redefined); validate_shape/1 (structural precondition, no I/O); compute_hash/2 -- SHA-256 hex (lowercase) over script_id <> 0x00 <> (canonicalized, deduped-via-Capabilities.new/1, lexicographically-sorted capabilities joined by 0x0A) <> 0x00 <> raw script_source, exactly per design doc §4.2; validate_at_load/3 -- pure, zero-dependency load-time gate (no call into Executor or LuaScriptAudit) that runs validate_shape/1 first, then compares compute_hash/2's output against a caller-supplied registered_hash, returning {:ok, hash} or {:error, {:manifest_mismatch, ...}} / {:error, {:invalid_manifest, ...}}. Moduledoc states the SHA-256/lowercase-hex algorithm and the exact byte layout (0x00/0x0A separators, canonicalization), and states R-Co's src/lua/manifest.zig is absent from this checkout (confirmed by find) so no field is named 'deliberately dropped' (OQ-1, matching REQ-157's precedent).

Extended lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex per the design's §5.3/§5.3.1 coordinated-change requirement: script_ref widened to accept either a bare binary() (legacy shape, treated as paired with an empty manifest %Manifest{script_id: "", capabilities: []} so every hash this module returns is uniformly Manifest.compute_hash/2's output, keeping every pre-REQ-158 bare-binary caller -- REQ-153/154/155/156's own ~40 existing test call sites -- compiling and passing unchanged) or a %{manifest: Manifest.t(), script_source: binary()} map carrying a real manifest. A script_ref matching neither shape returns {:error, :invalid_script_ref} without invoking the Lua runtime. run_script/3 (was run_script/2) and run_with_heap_limit/5 (was /4) both now take the manifest through and call Manifest.compute_hash(manifest, script_source) directly -- no byte-layout logic duplicated in executor.ex. Verified LuaScriptAudit.verify_manifest_hash/2 (INV-LSA-2) is untouched and still the sole comparison LuaScriptAudit performs; Manifest.validate_at_load/3 is a structurally separate, independent gate (INV-MAN-2/INV-MAN-3) that never calls into LuaScriptAudit or Executor.

Updated test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs's two hash-value-dependent tests (previously asserting a bare SHA-256(script_source)) to compute expected hashes via Manifest.compute_hash/2 over the implicit empty manifest, and added a new 'REQ-158: manifest-aware script_ref' describe block proving the map-shaped script_ref produces Manifest.compute_hash/2's exact output, that a capability-list change changes the returned hash, and that a malformed script_ref returns {:error, :invalid_script_ref}. Every other pre-existing test in that file (REQ-153/154/155/156, ~50 tests) is unchanged and still passes.

New test/letflow/engine/lua/manifest_test.exs (pure, async: true, no DB, per design's own file-layout note): struct/shape validation, hash determinism/canonicalization (order-insensitive, duplicate-insensitive), hash sensitivity (script_id, capabilities, script_source each independently change the hash), validate_at_load/3's modified-manifest rejection and unmodified-pair success, and AC2's ordering proof in two forms: (a) a bare recording-function double that is never invoked when validate_at_load/3 rejects, confirmed via refute_received; (b) a real-Executor call that is never made at all when the caller respects the load-time rejection -- proven by never reaching the Executor.execute_with_manifest call and asserting only Manifest's own {:manifest_mismatch, ...} error is observed (a script `error('this must never run')` would surface a distinguishable plain-string error if the Executor were ever wrongly invoked). Also asserts moduledoc content per AC5/AC6.

New test/letflow/engine/lua/manifest_executor_audit_test.exs (added beyond owned_modules; justified because AC3/AC4's end-to-end proof requires a real Postgres tenant schema for LuaScriptAudit.execute_script_for_audit/6's insert, which the design's own file-layout note excludes from the pure manifest_test.exs -- mirrors test/letflow/engine/lua_script_audit_test.exs's own provisioned_tenant/0 helper shape exactly, async: false, Letflow.DataCase): (a) AC3 -- a real Executor + real LuaScriptAudit call's persisted AuditRecord.manifest_hash equals Manifest.compute_hash/2's output for the executed manifest+script pair, confirmed by both the function's own return value and an independent Repo.get read-back; (b) AC4 -- an arbitrary wrong registered_hash yields LuaScriptAudit's own {:manifest_hash_mismatch, registered_hash, actual_hash} and writes zero audit rows; (c) AC4 race variant -- Manifest.validate_at_load/3 succeeding once against an original manifest does not suppress or substitute for LuaScriptAudit's own independent post-execution check when the manifest actually executed has since changed (stale registered_hash), still producing LuaScriptAudit's own mismatch error and zero rows.

Self-review checklist: no tenant-input SQL interpolation (N/A, this requirement adds no SQL); no unresolved {:ok, _} = match on an externally-reachable path (validate_at_load/3 and compute_hash/2 return tagged tuples/plain values pattern-matched explicitly everywhere they're called in this change); every new public function (Manifest.validate_shape/1, compute_hash/2, to_grant_set/1, validate_at_load/3) has a @doc; grepped lib/ for every real call site of Executor.execute_with_manifest/2,3 outside executor.ex itself -- only lib/letflow/engine/lua_script_audit.ex references it, via the unmodified, opaque-term() Executor behaviour callback, which required no change (executor.ex's script_ref type widening is entirely internal to the concrete Executor module, exactly as design §5.3.1 states). No migrations needed, none added. No change to lib/letflow/engine/lua/capabilities.ex or platform.ex.
result.handoff_note_for_reviewers: Design decision surfaced during implementation, not silently made: script_ref widened to accept EITHER a bare binary() (legacy -- implicitly paired with an empty manifest so its hash is still uniformly Manifest.compute_hash/2's output) OR a %{manifest:, script_source:} map, rather than requiring every caller to switch to the map shape immediately. This keeps ~40 pre-existing REQ-153/154/155/156 test call sites (all passing bare binaries) compiling and passing unchanged, while still fully satisfying REQ-158's AC3 (manifest-covering hash reaches the audit row) and AC1/AC2 (load-time rejection) via the map shape. Flagging for REVIEWER: is a permanent legacy bare-binary path acceptable, or should a future requirement force all callers onto the manifest-carrying map shape and delete the bare-binary clause? Not resolved here -- OQ-2/OQ-4 in the design doc already flag that no production caller of validate_at_load/3 or the manifest-carrying execute_with_manifest exists yet.
